cues.en: It's America's favorite chocolate bar. It's certainly my chocolate bar but to a great many people from other parts of the world, the Hershey bar tastes like vomit.
cues.zh: 这是全美最爱的巧克力棒。这当然也是我的巧克力棒，但对世界很多其他地方的人来说，Hershey bar 尝起来像呕吐物。

cues.en: Not figurative vomit but literal actual human sick. My wife Lauren knows what I'm talking about. When I was in college, worked at this camp in Pennsylvania and we took the kids to Hershey Park and my co counselor who is from New Zealand was very excited. She tried a Hershey kiss
cues.zh: 不是比喻意义上的呕吐物，而是真正的人类呕吐物。我妻子 Lauren 知道我在说什么。我上大学时，在宾夕法尼亚州的一个营地工作，我们带孩子们去 Hershey Park，我那位来自新西兰的搭档辅导员非常兴奋。她尝了一颗 Hershey kiss

cues.en: and promptly said,
cues.zh: 然后马上说：

cues.en: oh my god, this tastes like vomit. And then she made us all eat Cadbury.
cues.zh: 天啊，这尝起来像呕吐物。然后她逼我们所有人都吃 Cadbury。

cues.en: I talked about the Hershey bar recently on my TikTok, and look at all of these comments from people not in The US. And it's not just the Hershey bar. Hershey's has been so dominant in The US market for so long that most other big chocolate brands here have to imitate that Hershey taste to some extent. This is just what American consumers expect chocolate to taste like. But why? Well, the history and science that explains this is pretty interesting, and it raises some profound questions about how we define the quality of food. Is there such a thing as objectively
cues.zh: 我最近在TikTok上聊了好时巧克力棒，看看这些来自美国以外的评论。而且不只是好时巧克力棒。好时在美国市场称霸太久了，以至于这里大多数其他大巧克力品牌都不得不在某种程度上模仿好时的味道。美国消费者期待的就是这个味道。但为什么呢？解释这一点的历史和科学相当有意思，也引发了关于我们如何定义食物品质的深刻问题。食物是否存在客观上的

cues.en: good or bad food?
cues.zh: 好坏之分呢？

cues.en: Especially when it comes to something like a dessert, the sole function of which is to provide us with pleasure. The reason this tastes like puke to some people and this doesn't probably has to do with the milk, so we first have to understand how milk got into chocolate in the first place. For virtually all of its four thousand year history, chocolate has been a beverage.
cues.zh: 尤其是像甜点这样的东西，它唯一的作用就是给我们带来愉悦。这种东西对某些人来说尝起来像呕吐物，而那种不会，原因可能和牛奶有关；所以我们得先弄明白，牛奶最初是怎么进到巧克力里的。在它四千年历史中，几乎全程巧克力都是一种饮料。

cues.en: Ancient Mesoamericans
cues.zh: 古代中美洲人

cues.en: harvested cacao beans and did various things to combine them with water into a drink with medicinal and ceremonial
cues.zh: 采集可可豆，并用各种方式把它们与水混合成一种具有药用和仪式

cues.en: purposes. This may have included fermenting the cacao to make alcohol.
cues.zh: 用途的饮品。这可能包括发酵可可来制作酒精饮料。

cues.en: Europeans got chocolate by way of the Aztecs whom the Spanish conquered in the sixteenth century.
cues.zh: 欧洲人是从阿兹特克人那里得到巧克力的，而西班牙人在16世纪征服了阿兹特克人。

cues.en: The Spaniards used it as a medicine too, which makes sense because unsweetened cocoa totally tastes like medicine.
cues.zh: 西班牙人也把它当药用，这很合理，因为不加糖的可可尝起来完全就像药。

cues.en: It is crazy bitter. But as the song goes, a spoonful of sugar helps the medicine go down. And once somebody at the Spanish court got the bright idea to try that, Europeans started drinking chocolate for pleasure. And at some point, they also started pouring milk into their water based cocoa drink, the same way that people pour it into coffee.
cues.zh: 它苦得要命。但就像歌里唱的，一勺糖能让药好咽下去。西班牙宫廷里有人灵机一动试了这个办法后，欧洲人就开始为了享受而喝巧克力了。后来某个时候，他们也开始往水冲的可可饮料里加牛奶，就像人们往咖啡里加牛奶一样。

cues.en: It smooths and thickens the texture and it rounds off the bitter flavors. It wasn't until the nineteenth century that European confectioners started playing with solid chocolate products consisting of cocoa powder known as cocoa solids,
cues.zh: 它能柔化并增稠口感，还能缓和苦味。直到19世纪，欧洲糖果师才开始尝试固体巧克力产品，其成分包括可可粉（即可可固形物）、

cues.en: cocoa fat known as cocoa butter, and sugar, and eventually
cues.zh: 可可脂，以及糖，并最终

cues.en: milk for the same reason they put it in the drink. This was probably particularly advantageous for early solid chocolates which were produced by relatively crude means.
cues.zh: 加入牛奶——原因和他们往饮品里加牛奶一样。这对早期固体巧克力可能尤其有利，因为当时的生产方式相当粗糙。

cues.en: We love a milk free dark chocolate these days, but the original dark chocolate was often described as gritty and harsh. Adding milk helped. Contrary to what the Cadbury marketing illustrations would have you believe, you can't pour milk into solid chocolate. Milk is mostly water which doesn't mix with fat and confections with high water content are hospitable to microbial life. They can mold if you don't eat them within a few days. The Nestle company was born in Switzerland when Henri Nestle figured out a process to create dehydrated
cues.zh: 如今我们很爱无奶黑巧克力，但最早的黑巧克力常被形容为粗糙又刺口。加奶改善了口感。与 Cadbury 营销插画会让你相信的相反，你不能把牛奶倒进固体巧克力里。牛奶主要成分是水，而水不与脂肪混合；高含水量的甜食又容易滋生微生物。几天内吃不完就可能发霉。Henri Nestle 想出一种制造脱水

cues.en: milk, powdered milk. Nestle's neighbor Daniel Peter added the powdered milk to his solid chocolate mix and the rest is history.
cues.zh: 牛奶，也就是奶粉的工艺时，Nestle 公司在瑞士诞生了。Nestle 的邻居 Daniel Peter 把奶粉加入他的固体巧克力混合物，之后的事就人尽皆知了。

cues.en: Up in England, Cadbury's first solid milk chocolate also used powdered milk, But chocolatiers quickly figured out that you could make an even smoother tastier product if you used condensed milk rather than powdered milk. That is milk that has had a lot of its water boiled out, but it's still a liquid.
cues.zh: 在英格兰，吉百利的第一款固体牛奶巧克力用的也是奶粉，但巧克力制造商很快发现，用炼乳代替奶粉能做出更丝滑、更美味的产品。炼乳就是把大量水分煮掉，但它仍然是液体。

cues.en: Over in The United States, an already wealthy and successful caramel maker named Milton Hershey was trying to develop his own milk chocolate process.
cues.zh: 而在美国，一位已经相当富有且事业有成的焦糖制造商米尔顿·好时，正试图开发自己的牛奶巧克力工艺。

cues.en: Much of what I'm about to tell you is drawn from the journalist Michael D'Antonio's
cues.zh: 我接下来要讲的很多内容，都来自记者 Michael D'Antonio 的

cues.en: excellent biography of Hershey. In nineteen o three, Hershey retreated to his old family homestead in Pennsylvania and started experimenting
cues.zh: 那本关于 Hershey 的出色传记。1903 年，Hershey 回到位于 Pennsylvania 的家族旧宅，开始尝试

cues.en: with milk.
cues.zh: 用牛奶。

cues.en: The first thing that he landed on was using skim milk, milk that has had the fat removed. Milk fat would go rancid in the chocolate after a while, and that was not gonna work for the kind of shelf stable mass produced product that Hershey envisioned.
cues.zh: 他最先想到的是使用脱脂牛奶，也就是去掉脂肪的牛奶。乳脂在巧克力里放一段时间会变质，而这不适合 Hershey 设想的那种耐储存、可大规模生产的产品。

cues.en: He cooked batch after batch of milk in a giant copper vacuum pan. When you cook a liquid in a vacuum, that lowers its boiling point so you can drive off the water at much lower temperatures. He still couldn't get a product that he was happy with and in desperation one day Hershey summoned one of his factory workers named John Schmalbach.
cues.zh: 他在一个巨大的铜制真空锅里煮了一批又一批牛奶。在真空里煮液体能降低沸点，所以可以在低得多的温度下把水分蒸发掉。他还是做不出满意的产品，绝望之下，有一天 Hershey 叫来了工厂里一名叫 John Schmalbach 的工人。

cues.en: Schmalbach tried mixing the skim milk with sugar and then he cooked it on the vacuum pan at a very very low temperature for a long time. And then when it was done cooking,
cues.zh: Schmalbach 试着把脱脂牛奶和糖混合，然后在真空锅里用非常非常低的温度煮了很久。等煮好后，

cues.en: he turned off the heat and then just let it sit there and cool in the vacuum for a long time. Then they opened up the pan and Hershey said, look at that beautiful batch of milk. How come you didn't burn it? You didn't go to college. Out of context, that remark sounds way more rude than it probably actually was because just before this Hershey had indeed invited a fancy college chemist to his lab to try to make a batch of milk and the chemist did in fact burn that batch of milk. But anyway, Hershey and his guys made a batch of chocolate with small box milk and he thought it was perfect. The chocolate had a snap to it like al dente pasta. It was smooth, it was shelf stable,
cues.zh: 他关掉加热，让它在真空里静置冷却很长时间。然后他们打开锅，Hershey 说，看看这批多漂亮的牛奶。你怎么没把它烧焦？你又没上过大学。脱离语境听，这话比实际大概无礼得多，因为就在这之前，Hershey 确实请过一位名校化学家来实验室做一批牛奶，而那位化学家确实把那批牛奶烧焦了。但不管怎样，Hershey 和他的人用小盒装牛奶做了一批巧克力，他觉得完美极了。这巧克力咬下去有清脆的断裂感，像弹牙的意面。它口感顺滑，耐储存，

cues.en: and it was better suited to mass production.
cues.zh: 而且它更适合大规模生产。

cues.en: Condensed milk you can flow through systems of pipes, you can't do that with powdered milk. It may indeed have tasted a little like sick, we'll talk about why in a second, but Hershey had found a money saving product and process And you can save even more money on your groceries today with Fetch Rewards, the sponsor of this video whom I'll now briefly thank. Fetch is an incredibly easy way to convert your grocery shopping into savings on like almost any product you could think of. Here's how it works. You just hit my link in the description and download the app. Then whenever you go grocery shopping, you scan your receipt with your phone. It's really easy. The app tells you exactly what to do. You just follow the directions.
cues.zh: 炼乳可以通过管道系统流动，奶粉就不行。它尝起来可能确实有点像呕吐物，原因我们稍后再说，但 Hershey 找到了一种省钱的产品和工艺。而今天，通过 Fetch Rewards，你还能在食品杂货上省更多钱；它是本视频的赞助商，我现在简短致谢。Fetch 是一种极其简单的方式，能把你日常买菜变成几乎任何你能想到商品的优惠。它是这样运作的：点击简介里的链接并下载应用。之后每次去买菜，用手机扫描收据即可。非常简单。应用会明确告诉你怎么做，你照着指引操作就行。

cues.en: Even easier is uploading e receipts. That works for all kinds of online shopping, not just groceries. It scans your email for eligible receipts and then converts them into points. Points you can use on a million things. The app shows you restaurants,
cues.zh: 更简单的是上传电子收据。这对各种网购都有效，不只是食品杂货。它会扫描你的邮箱，找出符合条件的收据，再转换成积分。这些积分可以用在无数东西上。这个应用会给你展示餐厅、

cues.en: Apple iTunes or Google Play, clothes, electronics, anything
cues.zh: Apple iTunes 或 Google Play、服装、电子产品，任何

cues.en: on Amazon.
cues.zh: Amazon 上的东西。

cues.en: You send them your receipts, they send you points to save money. It's as simple as that, and you can get started right now with 2,000 points from me if you follow my link in the description and enter my code Regusia when you scan your first receipt. That's all down in the description. Thank you, Fetch. Now back to vomit chocolate.
cues.zh: 你把收据发给他们，他们给你积分，让你省钱。就这么简单。你只要点简介里的链接，并在扫描第一张收据时输入我的代码 Regusia，现在就能用我送的 2,000 积分开始。这些都在简介里。谢谢你，Fetch。现在回到呕吐巧克力。

cues.en: The thing about the low temperature reduction process that John Schmalbach had invented for Hershey
cues.zh: John Schmalbach 为 Hershey 发明的低温还原工艺，问题在于

cues.en: is that it soured the milk. Hershey's recipe is of course a closely guarded trade secret, but chocolate experts these days are generally in agreement that the sour taste in Hershey's is butyric acid, butter acid. They create it by lipolyzing
cues.zh: 它会让牛奶变酸。Hershey 的配方当然是被严守的商业秘密，但如今的巧克力专家普遍认为，Hershey 巧克力里的酸味来自丁酸，也就是黄油酸。他们通过脂解

cues.en: or breaking down the fat content in the milk. And butyric acid may very well have been what made that 19 o three batch of milk taste sour too. One way to make butyric acid is through anaerobic fermentation.
cues.zh: 也就是分解牛奶中的脂肪来产生这种酸。丁酸很可能也正是让 1903 年那批牛奶尝起来发酸的东西。生成丁酸的一种方法是厌氧发酵。

cues.en: Remember, they were doing it in a vacuum pan, anaerobic. Butyric acid is also created in our digestive systems. And in the event that the contents of our digestive systems
cues.zh: 记住，他们是在真空锅中、厌氧条件下做的。丁酸也会在我们的消化系统中生成。而如果消化系统里的东西

cues.en: leave,
cues.zh: 排出来，

cues.en: we are then exposed to that signature twang,
cues.zh: 我们就会接触到那种标志性的酸味，

cues.en: that smell, that taste of butyric acid. This is probably why people who didn't grow up eating this stuff think this tastes like sick.
cues.zh: 那种气味，那种丁酸的味道。这可能就是为什么从小不吃这东西的人觉得它尝起来像呕吐物。

cues.en: For me who did grow up eating this stuff, it's very different because I've eaten Hershey's chocolate way more often than I've thrown up, thankfully. Therefore to me, butyric acid tastes like chocolate, not sick. And when I go to the British import section of my local grocery store and pick up some goodies, Damn, no Aero bars today. I am usually struck by how this chocolate tastes flat to me, dull. It lacks the acidity that I've been conditioned to expect.
cues.zh: 对我这种从小吃这东西长大的人来说，感觉完全不同，因为谢天谢地，我吃 Hershey's 巧克力的次数远比呕吐多得多。所以对我来说，丁酸尝起来像巧克力，而不是呕吐物。而当我去本地杂货店的英国进口区挑零食时——该死，今天没有 Aero bars——我通常会被一个感觉击中：这巧克力对我来说太平淡、太乏味了。它缺少我已经习惯期待的那种酸味。

cues.en: And British chocolate in particular tends to taste kinda fatty to me. Indeed, Cadbury uses vegetable oils in addition to cocoa butter that may contribute to the smoother creamier texture Cadbury has relative to Hershey's, that could be a lot of things. The churning, the tempering, lots of things. Certainly, Cadbury lovers really value the comparatively creamy texture.
cues.zh: 尤其是英国巧克力，对我来说尝起来总有点油脂感偏重。确实，Cadbury 除了可可脂还使用植物油，这可能让它的口感比 Hershey's 更顺滑、更绵密；不过原因可能有很多。搅拌、调温，很多因素。当然，喜欢 Cadbury 的人确实很看重这种相对绵密的口感。

cues.en: I should acknowledge that this particular bar is the American version of the Cadbury dairy milk, which is ironically distributed and partially manufactured by Hershey's, and the recipe has been adjusted a bit for The US market. It has no vegetable oil in it because that's not legally allowed in a US product that's labeled as chocolate. It still tastes very different from a Hershey bar. Hershey haters often describe the texture of this as waxy by comparison to this, but you know what? I kinda like that. Cocoa butter goes very waxy when you get it cold as anyone who's had chocolate chip ice cream can tell you and I keep my chocolate bars in the fridge. I love that snap of waxy cocoa butter.
cues.zh: 我得说明，这块是美版的 Cadbury Dairy Milk，讽刺的是，它由 Hershey's 分销，并部分由 Hershey's 生产，配方也为美国市场做了些调整。里面没有植物油，因为美国法规不允许标为巧克力的产品添加植物油。它的味道仍然和 Hershey 巧克力棒很不一样。讨厌 Hershey's 的人常说，和这块相比，Hershey's 的口感像蜡一样；但你知道吗？我还挺喜欢那种感觉。可可脂变冷后会很有蜡感，吃过巧克力豆冰淇淋的人都懂，而我就把巧克力棒放在冰箱里。我喜欢那种蜡质可可脂带来的脆响。

cues.en: In
cues.zh: 在

cues.en: 2015, the BBC did a fun little focus group to analyze the difference between Hershey's and Cadbury and that strikes me as a fair comparison. They're both inexpensive mass produced mass market chocolates. It would be absurd to put a Hershey bar up against a fine handcrafted European chocolate. The adult focus groups preferred Cadbury. They described the Hershey's as harder, more bitter, not as rich.
cues.zh: 2015年，BBC做了一个有趣的小型焦点小组，分析Hershey's和Cadbury的差异，我觉得这是个公平的比较。两者都是廉价、量产、面向大众市场的巧克力。拿Hershey's巧克力棒去和精细手工制作的欧洲巧克力比，会很荒唐。成人焦点小组更喜欢Cadbury。他们形容Hershey's更硬、更苦、不够浓郁。

cues.en: Interestingly though, when the Beeb asked British kids which chocolate they liked, the kids were more likely to choose the Hershey bar. I think this one's better. Now some of you are probably thinking right now, of course the kids like the Hershey bar better. The Hershey bar has got way more sugar. Not really though. The BBC investigation found that widespread belief is chiefly the result of different labeling regulations in The UK versus The US.
cues.zh: 不过有意思的是，当 BBC 问英国孩子喜欢哪种巧克力时，孩子们更可能选 Hershey bar。我觉得这一款更好。现在你们有些人可能正在想，孩子们当然更喜欢 Hershey bar。Hershey bar 的糖分高多了。不过其实并不是这样。BBC 的调查发现，这种普遍看法主要是英国和美国标签法规不同造成的。

cues.en: Cadbury and Hershey have about the same proportion of sugar. It's just that milk comes higher on the Cadbury ingredients list because the Brits rank the milk based on its liquid weight not its evaporated weight. It may indeed be the case that the Hershey bar has proportionally less cocoa in it. If you look at The US and EU regulations on the minimum cocoa content of chocolate,
cues.zh: Cadbury 和 Hershey 的糖比例大致相同。只是牛奶在 Cadbury 的配料表里排得更靠前，因为英国人按牛奶的液体重量而不是蒸发后的重量来排序。Hershey 巧克力棒里的可可比例确实可能更低。如果你看美国和欧盟关于巧克力最低可可含量的法规，

cues.en: it looks like the EU standard is higher. Yes, The UK isn't a member of the EU anymore, but they're still generally operating under those old rules. The EU standard for the minimum cocoa content of milk chocolate is higher, but the European standard is for dry cocoa solids, whereas The US standard is for chocolate liquor which is a wet product. So these are probably apples and oranges numbers, I don't really know how to interpret this. I do know that a Hershey spokesman told the BBC that Hershey's contains 30% cocoa solids.
cues.zh: 看起来欧盟标准更高。是的，英国已经不是欧盟成员国了，但总体上仍在沿用那些旧规则。欧盟对牛奶巧克力最低可可含量的标准更高，但欧洲标准针对的是干可可固形物，而美国标准针对的是巧克力浆，这是一种湿性产品。所以这些数字可能根本没法直接比较，我也不太清楚该怎么解读。我确实知道，Hershey 的一位发言人告诉 BBC，Hershey's 含有 30% 的可可固形物。

cues.en: If true, that'd be higher than the 23% that Cadbury claims for their own product. Though he's probably talking about The UK version of the Hershey bar, which is a slightly different recipe. But it's certainly the case that a Hershey bar has way less cocoa in it than a fine European dark chocolate bar. I mean, look at it. Cocoa is very expensive and it's got a very intense flavor. Both of those things are bad for mass market chocolate. So if this doesn't have much cocoa in it, does that mean that the Hershey bar is an objectively inferior product?
cues.zh: 如果属实，那会比 Cadbury 声称自家产品含有的 23% 还高。不过他说的可能只是英国版的 Hershey bar，配方略有不同。但可以肯定的是，Hershey bar 的可可含量远低于优质欧洲黑巧克力棒。我是说，看看它就知道了。可可很贵，而且风味非常浓烈。这两点对大众市场巧克力都不利。所以，如果它的可可含量不高，那是否意味着 Hershey bar 是客观上更差的产品？

cues.en: Certainly, lot of people on my TikTok tried to make that argument. Cocoa is the defining ingredient of chocolate, so chocolate with less cocoa is objectively
cues.zh: 当然，我 TikTok 上有很多人试图提出这个论点。可可是巧克力的决定性成分，所以可可更少的巧克力客观上

cues.en: lesser chocolate because it's less chocolate. Interesting argument. Certainly, you would reach a point where the proportion of the cocoa was so low that the product would be utterly unrecognizable
cues.zh: 是更次的巧克力，因为它巧克力更少。有意思的论点。当然，你会达到一个点，可可比例低到产品完全无法被认出

cues.en: as chocolate. And some might argue that this has gone well below that point. But what if we extended that logic in the opposite direction? This logic implies that the finest chocolate bar in the world is the one that has the highest proportion of cocoa. And you know what? I happen to have some of that right here. It's called unsweetened
cues.zh: 是巧克力。有人可能会说，这已经远远低于那个点了。但如果我们把这种逻辑往相反方向延伸呢？这种逻辑意味着，世界上最好的巧克力棒就是可可比例最高的那根。你猜怎么着？我这儿正好有一些。它叫无糖

cues.en: baking chocolate. You ever just eaten some of this? Yeah. Eat that, and you will be immediately reminded why people started putting other stuff in their chocolate. You could argue that alcohol is the defining ingredient of a spirit. Right? And if we apply our chocolate logic to booze,
cues.zh: 烘焙巧克力。你有没有直接吃过这种？吃过。吃一口，你就会立刻想起为什么人们开始往巧克力里加别的东西。你可以说酒精是烈酒的决定性成分。对吧？如果我们把巧克力逻辑套到酒上，

cues.en: that means that pure ethanol is a superior beverage to fine Scotch whiskey, which has all kinds of other things in it besides ethanol.
cues.zh: 这意味着纯乙醇是比上等苏格兰威士忌更优的饮品，而后者除了乙醇还含有各种其他成分。

cues.en: And wine has even less alcohol in it than whiskey. Does that mean that whiskey is objectively superior to wine? Okay. Now you might say forget the cocoa percentages.
cues.zh: 葡萄酒的酒精含量还比威士忌更低。那这是否意味着威士忌客观上优于葡萄酒？好吧。现在你可能会说，先别管可可含量百分比了。

cues.en: Hershey bars are objectively bad because they taste like human vomit.
cues.zh: Hershey 巧克力棒客观上很差，因为味道像人的呕吐物。

cues.en: We are evolved to find certain tastes and smells repulsive
cues.zh: 我们进化得会对某些味道和气味感到厌恶

cues.en: because they are indicative of substances that are dangerous to us. We are evolved to be repulsed by butyric acid and therefore a food that contains butyric acid is a violation of natural law. Well, I happen to be a fan of violating what a lot of people regard as natural laws. And a lot of the world's great foods are great because they ride the line between enticement and revulsion.
cues.zh: 因为它们表明这些物质对我们有危险。我们进化得会对丁酸感到厌恶，因此含有丁酸的食物就违反了自然法则。嗯，我碰巧很喜欢违反许多人心目中的自然法则。而且世界上许多伟大的食物之所以伟大，是因为它们游走在诱惑与厌恶的边界上。

cues.en: Europeans generally love fermented milk products, think of all the stinky cheeses they dig and guess what, parmesan has butyric acid in it too. Certainly you could argue that food can be objectively bad from a nourishment perspective but even that would depend on the subjective
cues.zh: 欧洲人普遍喜欢发酵乳制品，想想他们爱吃的那些臭奶酪，而且你知道吗，Parmesan里也含有丁酸。当然，你可以说从营养角度看，食物有客观的好坏之分，但即便如此，这也要取决于主观的

cues.en: needs of the individual and that whole line of inquiry is moot when it comes to a dessert, it comes to candy that has no nutritional purpose.
cues.zh: 个人需求；而面对甜点、面对毫无营养价值的糖果时，这整条思路就根本站不住脚了。

cues.en: It's purely for pleasure and I derive a lot of pleasure from eating this not the least because I grew up with it. Candy more than anything else is wrapped up in childhood memory, right? I grew up in Central Pennsylvania not far from where Milton Hershey lived. There's an amusement park there now called Hershey Park. Every summer my parents would take me there to ride the roller coasters on the way out they would buy me a giant novelty Hershey kiss and I would slowly nibble away on that all summer long. Those warm feelings are half of what I'm tasting when I'm tasting this and I bet that you could think of a food that you could eat that would take you right back to a very happy place in your life. Life. In my moral code, anything that brings you pleasure is great so long as it doesn't come at the particular expense of anybody else or at the particular expense of your long term pleasure experiencing capacity.
cues.zh: 这纯粹是为了快乐，而吃它给我带来很大快乐，尤其因为我从小吃到大。糖果比任何东西都更与童年记忆绑在一起，对吧？我在宾夕法尼亚中部长大，离 Milton Hershey 住过的地方不远。那儿现在有个游乐园叫 Hershey Park。每年夏天父母都会带我去坐过山车，离开时他们会给我买一个巨型新奇 Hershey Kiss，我会整个夏天慢慢啃着吃。我品尝它时，尝到的一半就是这些温暖的感觉。我敢打赌，你也能想到一种食物，吃下去就能把你立刻带回人生中一个非常快乐的地方。人生。在我的道德准则里，任何给你带来快乐的东西都很好，只要它不是以损害某个特定他人为代价，也不是以损害你长期感受快乐的能力为代价。

cues.en: So take your pleasure where you find it, I'll do the same.
cues.zh: 所以，你在哪儿能找到快乐就在哪儿享受吧，我也会一样。
